evidence.note: Claim CONFIRMED: ci run --full on a ref equal to its base narrows the default pre-push command to sha^..sha (runner.py _default_on_the_diff sets since=sha^ when the base resolves to the ref, and scope_to_diff replaces --all-files with --from-ref sha^ --to-ref HEAD), so the pre-commit tests hook files: pattern skips it and --full runs zero tests but exits 0. Refuted if --full keeps --all-files. Probe: the new regression test in tests/test_ci_selected_scope.py failed on unfixed code with res.command ending in --from-ref <sha^> --to-ref HEAD (no --all-files), confirming the mechanism.

2 commits on branch ddflow/fix-B-ci-full-skips-tests-on-events-head: runner.py _default_on_the_diff gains full and override keyword-only flags -- it returns the command unchanged when full=True (a --full run always takes the whole suite) or override+no-changed_from (the operator's own --command runs as written); the caller passes full=full override=bool(command.strip()), so check_after_merge still scopes to its changed_from range. Two regression tests in tests/test_ci_selected_scope.py.

Loaded the rules digest via ddflow claim/brief for this item. Relevant rules applied: r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY from [REDACTED:path] before any gemini/google review -- required for the rubber_duck/critic cross-family review); r-task-phase-needs-wave (the fix task names its parent bugs-2 and carries wave:0). The bug-fix regression-test-first rule (a bug is not closed without a regression test that fails against the unfixed code) is honoured by the two new tests, which failed on the unfixed code and pass now.
